answer: Trust propagates through an attestation graph by bounded-length random walks, so endorsement influence depends on path probability rather than spreading without limit. A sybil cluster must connect to honest nodes through an external cut; if that cut is sparse, its conductance is low, limiting walk escape and trusted mass crossing the boundary. Under voting rules tied to that mass, min-cut bounds cap aggregate voting weight, even when grove, sable, and quill identities endorse one another densely.
